messages:
simon: Heads-up — after yesterday's runtime change the 8xA100 multi-GPU validation runs show a clear perf regression when using LL/LL128 + 4 NCCL channels. p99 token latency ~2.3x higher for long-context workloads. starting thread to collect signals.

maya: ugh. which workloads? long seqs only? any KV-cache involvement? :thinking_face:

simon: primarily long seq (2k+). KV cache enabled; we do the usual prefix caching. small batches (1-4) seem worst. seq length and small batch combo spikes.

priya: can you paste the run config and nccl settings? suspect channel scheduling + algo/proto mismatch.

simon: config dump:```yaml
model_parallel: tensor:2 pipeline:1
batching: min_batch=1 max_batch=4
nvlink: enabled
nccl:
  channels: 4
  enable_ll128: true
  algo: "tree"
  proto: "LL128"
```

simon: quick perf sample (tail):
```
2026-02-12 03:12:01 INFO tokens: 34
compute_ms: 12.4
comm_allreduce_ms: 23.8
comm_collective_wait_ms: 45.1
kv_lookup_ms: 2.1
overall_p99_ms: 210.6
```

anika: that collectives wait is huge. looks like allreduce queuing/serialization. do we have per-channel occupancy logs?

leo: I dumped NCCL traces with NCCL_DEBUG=TRACE for the failing run. pattern: channels 0..3 serialized rather than overlapped; many small allreduces back-to-back. suspect proto selection falling back to algo that can't do LL128 on certain tensor sizes.

priya: @simon can you rerun with `NCCL_ALGO=ring` and `NCCL_PROTO=Simple` just to compare? also try `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` so it's less noisy.

simon: running now. also toggling channels=1 and channels=8 to compare. will post numbers.

ci-bot: CI: perf-suite/8xA100 scheduled job #1123 started by simon (commit a1b2c3).

(20m later)

simon: quick results: baseline (channels=4, LL128/tree): p99 210ms. channels=1 p99 120ms. channels=8 p99 190ms. NCCL_ALGO=ring + proto=Simple p99 125ms.

maya: interesting — channels=1 best. means channel contention/scheduling is worse than single-channel ring for our small-batch long-seq pattern.

anika: Could be that our kernel selection emits lots of tiny gradients that cause many tiny allreduces. With channels>1, the runtime splits into multiple small collectives which creates queueing. Single channel batches them in a single larger collective.

priya: Agreed. Two mitigation vectors: 1) detect tiny collective sizes and prefer single-channel/ring for them; 2) adjust kernel selection to merge small comm ops (aggressive fusion).

leo: also saw fallback messages in traces: `ncclGetAlgo: requested LL128 but falling back to Simple for size=...` — so actual proto may be mismatched at runtime depending on tensor shape. runtime should log that and pick consistent fallback strategy.

simon: adding a lightweight heuristic: if mean allreduce bytes < 32KB, force channels=1 and NCCL_ALGO=ring for that step. anyone object?

priya: sounds reasonable as a short-term guardrail. need a perf test to validate cost per token vs throughput tradeoff.

anika: can we add a perf counter to the profiler: "mean_allreduce_bytes" per step and expose in console? that would make future triage faster.

priya: also add an eval job that runs long-context small-batch profile weekly to catch regressions.

leo: I'll open an RFC/PR for a fallback policy and add diagnostics to runtime logs. will include a sample of traces and the heuristic thresholds.

simon: action items:
- leo: RFC + instrumentation (traces + mean_allreduce_bytes) — due EOD tomorrow
- anika: prototype kernel fusion pass to merge small collectives — PoC in 1 week
- priya: add weekly perf job and alerts for p99 spike on long-seq small-batch — onboarding to alerts team
- simon: deploy guardrail: if mean_allreduce_bytes < 32KB set channels=1 for that request (hotfix)

priya: adding to roadmap. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: CI: perf-suite/8xA100 job #1123 completed — p99 regressed by 1.75x vs baseline; details in https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/1123

simon: will paste trace snippets and the PR link here when ready. closing loop in a follow-up message.
